# Covenant Day School — Course Offerings — Curriculum Guide

> **Provenance:** Compiled by Claude Code on 2026-08-15 from the school's High
> School Profile PDFs (course matrices, extracted with `pdftotext -layout`) and the
> academics pages. **High school only** — the Lower School and Middle School
> academics pages describe competencies, not named course lists, so no JK-5 or 6-8
> catalog exists to transcribe (confirmed absence).
>
> **⚠️ CORRECTION (2026-08-17) — the "confirmed absence" above is WRONG.** The
> Lower and Middle School academics pages DO publish per-grade curriculum, behind
> click-to-open tiles whose text is loaded by JavaScript and is absent from the
> page HTML a plain `curl` returns. That retrieval failure was mistaken for a
> publication gap. The real material is now captured in the three sibling files
> in this folder (`… - Lower School Curriculum.md`, `… - Middle School
> Curriculum.md`, `… - High School Course and Elective Offerings.md`), each
> recording the reproducible fetch. **This file is superseded for course lists**
> and retained only for the Profile-PDF material the academics pages do not carry
> (graduation units, weighting, AP gating, edition drift). Where this file and the
> academics-page files disagree on a course list, the academics pages win — they
> are the school's current self-published catalog.

### Sources

- 2026-2027 High School Profile (current course matrix — the primary source):
 https://resources.finalsite.net/images/v1758547252/covenant/x8i0qddxvctsp5jqbpmt/2025-26HSGuidanceProfile.pdf
- 2024-2025 High School Profile (broader matrix — AP Calc BC, AP Human Geography,
 AP French, Liberal Arts Math, Intro to Engineering appear here):
 https://resources.finalsite.net/images/v1726168257/covenant/jg1wjr67fw5ewgwy5bkz/2024-2025HSGuidanceProfilefinal_1.pdf
- 2023-24 High School Profile (explicit Honors and AP course lists):
 https://resources.finalsite.net/images/v1695399666/covenant/zogqb5jfwbqp0henpd36/HighSchoolProfileFINAL9-12.pdf
- https://www.covenantday.org/academics/high-school (department list)
- https://www.covenantday.org/academics (divisions are lower-school /
 middle-school / high-school; an /academics/upper-school URL 404s)

### Counting rules (decisions, recorded per the plan)

- **`us-courses` = 80** — level-qualified course entries in the 2026-2027 matrix
 (a title offered at CP, Honors and AP counts once per level, matching how the
 other schools' catalogs list courses). Distinct titles ≈ 65.
- **`advanced-courses` = 15 AP** — the 2026-2027 matrix's AP column. The school's
 own earlier editions ran higher (17 explicit APs in 2023-24; 18 in the 2024-2025
 matrix, adding Calculus BC, Human Geography, French); third-party counts
 (15-21) are superseded by the profile. The current-year figure is used.
- **`us-departments` = 9** — the 8 matrix disciplines (English, Mathematics,
 Science, Social Studies, World Language, Fine Arts, Restoration &
 Sustainability, PE) **plus Bible**, which has no matrix row but is a named
 subject area on the academics page and a 3-unit graduation requirement with a
 course every year.

### The 2026-2027 course matrix, transcribed

**English** — CP: Language & Literature · American Literature · Composition &
Literature · British Literature. Honors: Language & Literature · American
Literature · Composition & Literature · Literature & Philosophy*. AP: English
Language & Composition · English Literature & Composition.

**Mathematics** — CP: Algebra 1 · Algebra 2 · Geometry · Pre-Calculus ·
Statistics. Honors: Geometry · Algebra 2 · Pre-Calculus · Calculus* ·
Statistics*. AP: Calculus AB · Statistics.

**Science** — CP: Biology · Chemistry · Health · Sports & Exercise Science.
Honors: Biology · Chemistry · Anatomy · Sports & Exercise Science. AP: Biology ·
Chemistry · Environmental Science · Physics.

**Social Studies** — CP: World History · US History · Government & Economics.
Honors: World History · US History · Government & Economics · Psychology. AP:
US History · Government & Politics US · European History · Psychology.

**World Language** — CP: Latin 2 · Spanish 1 · Spanish 2 · French 1 · French 2.
Honors: Latin 3 · Latin 4 · Spanish 3 · Spanish 4 · French 3 · French 4. AP:
Latin · Spanish.

**Fine Arts** — CP: Choir · Symphonic Band · Theatre · Theatre Tech · Worship
Leadership · Intro to Art · Art 2D/3D · Ceramics · Digital Photography · Graphic
Design · Yearbook. Honors: Choir · Auditioned Theatre · Symphonic Band · Studio
Art · Yearbook. AP: Studio Art.

**Restoration & Sustainability** — Augustine Literacy Project · Intercultural
Practicum · Introduction to Engineering · Restore525.

**PE** — Strength & Fitness.

\* = available for **Dual Enrollment with Covenant College** (Honors Calculus,
Honors Statistics, Honors Literature & Philosophy).

### Structure and policy

- **25 Carnegie Units to graduate**: 4 English · 4 Math · 3 Science · 3 Social
 Studies · 3 Bible (a Bible course each year) · 1 Fine Art · 0.5 Health · 1 PE
 (earnable via two school sport seasons) · 5.5 electives.
- Weighted scale: 4.33 A+ base · Honors +0.5 · DE/AP +1.0. No class rank.
- AP gating: none for freshmen; sophomores max one; "two AP courses in the junior
 year and four AP courses senior year is a very demanding course load."
- Online partner: SevenStar Academy (transcript-noted).
- **Edition drift note:** the 2024-2025 matrix additionally carried AP Calculus BC
 ("course offering may be impacted by student enrollment"), AP Human Geography,
 AP French, CP Liberal Arts Math, CP Intro to Engineering (Science), CP Digital
 Storytelling, and ContainIt (R&S) — evidence the catalog flexes year to year
 around enrollment.

---

sections.text:
*(tile `post_id=666`, verbatim)*

Language Arts
Phonics: Demonstrate directionality (left-right), read all individual letters of the alphabet by saying the sounds correctly (phonics), read at least 10 digraphs, identify initial, end and medial sounds of words, read short vowel words using phonetic knowledge by sound blending (CVC), and read at least 5 common exception (sight) words
Reading Comprehension: Demonstrate understanding by answering and asking questions about a text, predict what might happen next in a story, retell stories in the correct sequence
Writing: Write most lowercase and capital letters using correct letter formation and write name using correct letter formation
Math
Shapes and Measurement:
Understand positional relationships
Identify and describe 2D shapes
Compare length, weight, and capacity using appropriate vocabulary
Number Sense:
Verbally count confidently to 20
Count out loud backward from 10 by 1s
Count up to 10 objects/Cardinal Principle
Automatically recall number bonds to 5
Automatically recall double facts to 10
Subitize to 5
Write numbers 1-10 using the correct formation
Patterns:
Identify and extend repeating patterns
Sort and classify by attributes (color, shape, size)
Compare quantities (<, >, =) up to 10
Bible
Students learn about God's love. Students memorize short Scripture passages and learn about key Bible characters and their stories. They also attend chapel every week and participate in lower school Missions Week.
Science and Social Studies
Students confidently explore the natural world, making appropriate comments and observations. They learn the names of parts of the body and important processes and changes in the world around them (seasons, life cycles, plant growth, and changing states of matter.) They also learn about significant historical figures, understand past, present, and future concepts, similarities and differences between life in their country and life in other countries, and appreciate community helpers.
Art
Students use their imagination to role-play activities and perform for an audience. Nursery rhymes and songs are a part of learning, along with various materials, tools, and art techniques.

---

sections.preview: *(tile `post_id=667`, verbatim)* Language Arts Phonics: Phonological awareness, short vowel words, and sight word recognition Reading Comprehension: Story retelling, listening comprehension, verbal reasoning and background knowledge Writing: Handwriting, sentence structure and punctuation, forming sentences, and…

Students learn concepts of measurements, adding and subtracting combinations of 10, graphing, estimating, and calendar components.
Bible
Students learn about friendship with God and others through group projects, activity centers, and community life in the classroom. They attend chapel each week and participate in the lower school Missions Week. Students memorize short Scripture passages and discover Bible characters and their stories.
Science
Students discover God’s awesome strength in the oceans, creative patterns through the seasons of the year, and animal life cycles.
Social Studies
Students learn about God's sovereign plan for the lives of people through the explorers, the pilgrims, and Native Americans and about His creativity through famous artists and holidays. Through a study of world cultures and traditions, students learn about empathy for others in light of the Gospel.

---

Language Arts
Phonics/Spelling: Phonological awareness, decoding, sight word recognition, fluency, and vocabulary.
Grammar: Parts of Speech: nouns (common, proper, singular, plural), verbs, adjectives, capitalization, punctuation and sentence types.
Reading Comprehension: Retelling, summarizing, visualizing, verbalizing, main idea and details, compare/contrast, cause/effect, classify/categorize, and fact/opinion.
Writing: Personal narratives, opinion, informational, and letter formation (printing).
Math
Using manipulatives, students learn place value to 100, numbers to 120, number bonds and tasks, addition and subtraction to 100, ordinal numbers, and position words. Students explore 2D and 3D shapes and patterns, mental math, customary measurement: length and weight, and math vocabulary. Students are introduced to picture and bar graphs and money and expand their knowledge of calendar and time skills.
Bible
Students study God’s truths through the lives of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, Joseph, Moses, the nation of Israel, and the settling of the Promised Land. Other Bible stories include Judges and Ruth, Samuel and Saul, King David and Solomon’s reigns, the divided kingdom, exile and return of Israel, Psalms, and Proverbs.
Science
Students examine seasonal patterns, plants, light and sound waves, animal behaviors, and habitats.
Social Studies
Students learn safety and laws and about responsible citizenship. Students engage in units about home, school and community, and map skills. They also gain an understanding of past, present, and future events.

---

sections.preview: *(tile `post_id=669`, verbatim)* Language Arts Phonics/Spelling: Phonological awareness, decoding and encoding short and long vowel words and multi-syllabic words, sight word recognition, fluency, and vocabulary Grammar: Parts of Speech (nouns-common, proper, singular, plural), verbs, adjectives; capitalization and…
sections.text:
*(tile `post_id=669`, verbatim)*

Language Arts
Phonics/Spelling: Phonological awareness, decoding and encoding short and long vowel words and multi-syllabic words, sight word recognition, fluency, and vocabulary
Grammar: Parts of Speech (nouns-common, proper, singular, plural), verbs, adjectives; capitalization and punctuation, sentence types and contractions
Reading Comprehension: Retelling, summarizing, visualizing and verbalizing, sequencing, main ideas and details, compare/contrast, cause/effect, classify/categorize, fact/opinion, language structure, verbal reasoning, and background knowledge to the text
Writing: Expanding personal narratives, opinion, information, and letter formation (printing and cursive)
Math
Students build on previous math experiences, strengthen number sense, fact families to 20, mental math and estimation, place value up to 1,000, and adding and subtracting 2 and 3 digit numbers. Students use math manipulatives throughout math units, including the introduction of fractions, multiplication and division, time and elapsed time, money, and customary and metric measurements. Students explore graphs, charts, line plots, and problem-solving strategies using word problems and math tools with bar models and picture representation.
Bible
Students review the Old Testament with the Jesse Tree and the inter testament time period.  The focus is on the New Testament, including Jesus’ birth, ministry, preaching, praying, miracles, parables, and the crucifixion and resurrection of Christ. Studies conclude with the early church and Paul’s ministry and missionary journeys.
Science
Students explore the human body, life cycles, insects, oceanography, animal behaviors, and interactions with matter.
Social Studies
Students study immigration, geography’s influence on communities, community helpers, globes and map skills, community resources and stewardship, holidays, and culture across the world. They also learn about how government officials are elected and how history contributes to a community’s heritage.

---

Grammar: Identify relationships among words, including synonyms, antonyms, homonyms, and multiple-meaning words, contractions, effective use of capitalization, punctuation, spelling,…
sections.text:
*(tile `post_id=670`, verbatim)*

Language Arts
Spelling: Encoding and decoding, patterns and rules, and syllable division.
Grammar: Identify relationships among words, including synonyms, antonyms, homonyms, and multiple-meaning words, contractions, effective use of capitalization, punctuation, spelling, adjectives/adverbs, prepositions, regular and irregular verbs, abstract nouns/pronouns, build and use accurately conversational, general academic, and content-specific words and phrases.
Reading Comprehension: Predicting, visualizing and verbalizing, summarizing, sequencing, inferring and drawing conclusions; compare/contrast, main ideas and details; cause/effect; author’s purpose, story elements, reading accuracy, fluency and expression, vocabulary and language structure.
Writing: Complete simple, compound and declarative, interrogative, imperative, and exclamatory sentences, using coordinating and subordinating conjunctions and interjections; classify and identify parts of a sentence and apply in composition (subject, verb, capital letter, end mark, makes complete sense), differentiate between a complete, sentence fragment, and run on sentence.
Math
Students learn place value to 10,000, rounding numbers, mental math and estimation, addition and subtraction to 10.000, bar models to solve word problems, deepen number sense, multiplication facts 0-12, multiplication and division of 1 and 2 digit numbers, fractions and decimals, angles and lines, area and perimeter, 3D and 2D shapes. Students expand their knowledge of money, time and elapsed time, customary metric measurement conversions, bar graphs, and line plots.
Bible
Students study creation, the fall, Noah, the Tower of Babel, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, the Exodus, the ten commandments, wandering in the wilderness, and the Promised Land. The year concludes with a Bible book study of Ephesians.
Science
Students learn about forces and magnetism, the earth and the activity on it, plants, animals, and fossils.
Social Studies
Students discover how events, individuals, and ideas have influenced communities, especially Charlotte, NC. Students learn about major landforms and their impact on people, industries, the economy, and the 13 American colonies.

---

sections.preview: *(tile `post_id=671`, verbatim)* Language Arts Spelling: Decoding and reading words by applying phonics and word analysis skills, fluency and accuracy when reading, building and applying vocabulary using various strategies and sources, applying knowledge of word structure elements, determining the meanings,…
sections.text:
*(tile `post_id=671`, verbatim)*

Language Arts
Spelling: Decoding and reading words by applying phonics and word analysis skills, fluency and accuracy when reading, building and applying vocabulary using various strategies and sources, applying knowledge of word structure elements, determining the meanings, pronunciations, syllabication, synonyms, antonyms, and parts of speech of words by using reference aids as glossaries, dictionaries, and thesauruses
Grammar: Morphology, spelling rules (suffixes, prefixes, base words, contractions, compound words, and syllables), types of sentences, punctuation, singular and possessive nouns, titles and quotation marks, parts of a sentence (subject, predicate, conjunctions, nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, pronouns, prepositional phrases, subject-verb agreement), editing/revising, styles of writing (informational, poetry, narrative, summary, creative, persuasive, literary analysis, author studies)
Reading Comprehension: Visualization and verbalization, vocabulary, verbal reasoning, language structure, summarizing, making corrections, inferring and predicting, asking questions, fact/opinion, author’s viewpoint, and character development and reading and comprehending a variety of literature independently and proficiently
Writing: Develop writing skills by writing for different purposes and to specific audiences and people (persuasive, informative, narrative, personal), produce coherent and legible documents by planning, drafting, revising, editing, and collaborating with others
Math
Students continue to build on math concepts, including number sense, addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division (facts, multi-digit numbers, common multiples, factors, estimation, and problem solving. Students master skills in the areas of mean, median, mode and range, fractions (adding and subtracting, equivalent, mixed numbers and improper), decimals (understanding, adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing), measurements (length, weight, volume, customary and metric, converting metric units), perimeter/area, lines, angles, quadrilaterals, other polygons, congruence and symmetry, bar models to solve multi-step word problems, money, time and time elapsed time.
Bible
Students study the book of Philippians, Judges, Joshua, King Saul, King David, King Solomon, Ruth, Samuel, the divided kingdom, the feast of trumpets, the day of atonement, and the fruit of the spirit.
Science
Students explore energy, speed, moving objects, waves, the earth’s features, natural hazards, structures, and functions.
Social Studies
Students study the state of North Carolina, including regions, history, government, and environmental and technological factors that affect the growth and development of the state.

---

sections.preview: *(tile `post_id=672`, verbatim)* Language Arts Grammar: Parts of speech (nouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs, pronouns, prepositions), suffixes/prefixes, analogies, contractions, compound words, singular/plural, subjects/predicates, identifying and writing complete sentences, punctuation/capitalization, prepositional…
sections.text:
*(tile `post_id=672`, verbatim)*

Language Arts
Grammar: Parts of speech (nouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs, pronouns, prepositions), suffixes/prefixes, analogies, contractions, compound words, singular/plural, subjects/predicates, identifying and writing complete sentences, punctuation/capitalization, prepositional phrases, clauses.
Reading Comprehension Predicting/inferring, visualizing/verbalizing, summarizing, sequencing, making connections, drawing conclusions, compare/contrast, identifying (main ideas, details cause/effect, author’s purpose, point of view, story elements, theme), genres (fiction, fantasy, biographies, history fiction, non-fiction, poetry), reading accuracy, fluency and expression, vocabulary and morphology.
Writing: Conventions (spelling, syllable division, writing mechanics), structure (identify audience, purpose, personal voice, writer’s viewpoint, organizing information, effective sentences - opening, closings combining, variety, elaboration - reasons, details, developing ideas, staying on topic, paragraphing - topic sentence, details, word choice - vivid, sensory details, description figurative language, writing process).Written expression includes descriptive, narrative, expository, persuasive writings, and literary analysis.
Math
Students master skills in place value to 10,000,000, mental math, estimation, multi-digit multiplication, division of numbers, fractions (adding and subtracting, equivalent, mixed numbers and improper), bar graph problem solving models, algebraic thinking, area/perimeter, ratios, decimals and percents, graphs, probability, types of angles, and number sense.
Bible
Students study the book of 1 Peter, Old Testament covenants, Judah’s return, writers of the Gospel and how the Gospels were written, Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, Jesus’ birth, early life and ministry, Hannukah, Jesus’ expanded ministry and growing popularity, Passover, parables, Jesus’ Galilean ministry, His death and resurrection, and His further ministry.
Science
Students discover chemical and physical property change, gravity, energy, photosynthesis and decomposition of plants and earth systems.
Social Studies
Students explore world and state geography, ancient Mesopotamia, ancient Greece and Rome, Vikings, Medieval Europe, Renaissance and the Reformation, Age of Exploration, Mayas, Incas, and Aztecs.

*(tile `post_id=673`, verbatim)*

Art
Skill, craftsmanship, beauty, clarity, balance, and other timeless elements are studied and practiced in lower school art classes. Art education sets students on a trajectory for understanding the beauty of Christ and His creation. Students practice painting, sketching, ceramics, printmaking, landscapes, portraits, and many other projects. The annual spring Art Walk event allows students to display their work for family and friends.
Music
The lower school music program exposes students to music in various ways. Vocal, instrumental, and percussion music is practiced while studying essential concepts like melody and rhythm through classical and modern composers. Fourth-grade students learn to play the recorder, while fifth-graders play band instruments. Vocal and instrumental concerts are held at Christmas and throughout the spring. 4th & 5th grade students interested in singing can join the children’s choir. In addition, private piano, vocal, and guitar lessons are available during school hours and after school.
CREATE Junior
CREATE Junior integrates technology and critical thinking skills with the content areas at each grade level. Students solve problems and build collaboration skills through science, technology, math, and engineering. CREATE Junior is a precursor to the CDS Middle School’s CREATE.
Spanish
The lower school Spanish program teaches children to learn the language and also to engage in the culture. Holidays, geography, and traditions of Spanish communities are studied.
Physical Education
Students flock to P.E. each week to practice various athletic skills and build endurance. The P.E. teacher encourages sportsmanship through encouragement and team building. Lessons center around developmentally appropriate skills. The Turkey Trot and Field Day are highlights for lower school students.
Library
The lower school library encourages the joy of reading and exploration of various genres. The librarian instructs students on how to find books and wisely develop their research skills in print and online. Students participate in the Readers Are Leaders program, which encourages them to read for pleasure with a purpose. The library team chooses literature with great intentionality and care.

---

sections.text:
*(tile `post_id=675`, verbatim)*

Language Arts
Students hone their skills in reading and writing. They practice reading deeply through synthesis and analysis of fiction and nonfiction texts. All students receive extra time of Applied English to become more familiar with how to write solid thesis statements, which build the foundation for strong essays.
Math
Students review arithmetic and basic number sense, including decimal and fraction operations, which prepare students for units of study in ratios and percentages. Additional units include integers, variables, equations and inequalities, 2 and 3-dimensional geometry, and statistics. Students focus on thinking logically, using various strategies and tools, communicating mathematical concepts effectively, and problem-solving.
Bible
Students study the Old Testament in this survey class. They build upon their knowledge of events and themes recorded within scripture to deepen their understanding of what the Bible teaches about God, humanity, and self. A Christian worldview for approaching every issue is developed from the study of scripture.
Science
Students study Life Science, which includes cells, heredity, DNA, viruses, bacteria, protists and fungi, animals, systems of the human body, plants, and dissection, allowing them to examine the phenomena of physical and living things as part of God’s plan. Teachers integrate lab experiments and projects designed to improve a student’s ability in critical thinking, creativity, communication, and collaboration.
Social Studies
Students embark on a comprehensive study of the history and geography of the United States, focusing on Jamestown Colony to the Civil War in US History Part 1. They investigate how humanity has responded to God’s call to care for and unfold the earth. Students learn central themes of formation by studying elements that shape cultures and countries.
World Languages
Students engage in Greek Mythology to begin their study of Latin in middle school. Through the discipline of language study, students’ perceptions and understandings of other cultures and their own are enriched. Spanish is offered as an elective.
Physical Education
Students acquire specific game skills and strategies and set personal fitness goals, emphasizing life sports and healthy living. Students in grades 7-8 may participate on Covenant Day athletic teams.

---

sections.text:
*(tile `post_id=676`, verbatim)*

Language Arts
Students continue the writing process, expanding the framework to apply their skills to persuasive, informative, narrative, and research-based writing styles. Students interact with complex texts and read for meaning from literature crucial to their learning and preparation for high school and college. They continue to develop their grammar skills through exposure to more complex concepts and continual review of basic grammar mechanics. The study of Greek and Latin roots guides students to have a deeper understanding of the vocabulary in literature. All students receive extra time of Applied English to develop their writing responses to texts.
ENGLISH HONORS
Students learn to perform deeper, more complex analyses of literature and written expression within the framework of a biblical worldview. Students build reading comprehension and critical thinking strategies to analyze the elements of literature, make inferences, recognize themes, and compare texts. The course teaches students to write a multi-paragraph argumentative essay with a thesis statement, textual evidence, and commentary. Students will learn to write expository essays and utilize appropriate transitions to create clarity and cohesion of ideas and concepts when writing. The use of standard written and oral English language conventions (punctuation, capitalization, grammar, and usage) is covered at an accelerated pace to strengthen communication skills.
Math
Students learn ratios and proportional relationships, unit conversions, integers throughout all mathematical operations, order of operations and expressions, continued development of equations and inequalities, geometry, statistics, and probability. Students focus on thinking logically, using various strategies and tools, communicating mathematical concepts effectively, and problem-solving.
MATH HONORS (Pre-Algebra)
Students are introduced to algebra through solving equations and inequalities, exponent rules, linear relations and functions, radicals, angle relationships, angles and polygons, and unit conversions. This course focuses on thinking logically, using various strategies and tools, communicating mathematical concepts effectively, and problem-solving.
Bible
Students study the Gospels. The teacher weaves the four books together to show students the life of Christ and his fulfillment of Scripture through His ministry, death, and glorious resurrection. Students learn how to study the Bible and are encouraged to develop the habit of personal devotions.
Science
Students study earth science, consisting of geology, oceanography, meteorology, and astronomy, allowing them to examine the phenomena of physical and living things as part of God’s plan. They integrate lab experiments and projects designed to improve a student’s ability in critical thinking, creativity, communication, and collaboration.
Social Studies
Students study the Reconstruction Era to the present day through a Biblical lens. The teacher uses interactive activities to build the students’ understanding of primary documents written by historical figures.
World Languages
Students engage in Latin IA to continue their study of Latin in middle school. Through the discipline of language study, students’ perceptions and understandings of other cultures and their own are enriched. Spanish is offered as an elective.
Physical Education
Students acquire specific game skills and strategies and set personal fitness goals, emphasizing life sports and healthy living. Students in grades 7-8 may participate on Covenant Day athletic teams.

---

sections.text:
*(tile `post_id=677`, verbatim)*

Language Arts
Students continue the writing process by applying their skills to informative, narrative, and research writing styles, culminating in a research paper. Students interact with complex texts and read for meaning from various literature crucial to their learning and preparation for high school and college. Students continue to develop their grammar skills through exposure to more complex concepts and continual review of basic grammar mechanics. Students learn to conduct cross-discipline research writing assignments to build competency in the research process.
ENGLISH HONORS
The goal of 8th grade Honors English is for students to develop a deeper understanding of how to use their biblical worldview as they study literature. Students will broaden their knowledge through rigorous literary analysis while working through major literary themes, history, and culture. They will become acquainted with authors representing different life experiences and relationships. They will improve their ability to read critically, make interpretive connections, and share ideas in discussions. Students will develop in-depth writing skills through multiple formal and informal responses, analytical essays, and creative pieces. Students will increase their awareness of syntax and expand their vocabulary.
Math
Students are introduced to algebra through solving equations and inequalities, exponent rules, linear relations and functions, radicals, angle relationships, angles and polygons, and unit conversions. This course focuses on thinking logically, using various strategies and tools, communicating mathematical concepts effectively, and problem-solving.
MATH HONORS (Algebra)
Students study the real numbers system, expressions, linear and quadratic equations, including their graphs, inequalities, systems of equations, polynomials, relations, functions, radical expressions and equations, and rational expressions. Introduces algebra through solving equations and inequalities, exponent rules, linear relations and functions, radicals, angle relationships, angles and polygons, and unit conversions. They focus on thinking logically, using various strategies and tools, communicating mathematical concepts effectively, and problem-solving.
Bible
Students study Acts and the Pauline Epistles. Teachers lead students to make practical applications in their lives. Students learn how to share their faith. The teacher encourages students to a deeper understanding of their faith through discussions.
Science
Students study physical science, learning about motion and forces, energy and waves (sound, light, and electricity), magnetism, and chemistry, allowing them to examine the phenomena of physical and living things as part of God’s plan. They integrate lab experiments and projects designed to improve a student’s ability in critical thinking, creativity, communication, and collaboration.
Social Studies
Students plunge into a comprehensive study of the history and geography of the world in World History Part 1. They investigate how humanity has responded to God’s call to care for and unfold the earth. Students study Mesopotamia, Ancient Egypt, Ancient Greece & Rome through the Middle Ages. Major world religions and how they relate to Christianity are covered in this course.
World Languages
Students engage in Latin IB to complete their Latin study in middle school. Through the discipline of language study, students’ perceptions and understandings of other cultures and their own are enriched. Spanish is offered as an elective.
Physical Education
Students acquire specific game skills and strategies and set personal fitness goals emphasizing life sports and healthy living. Students may participate on Covenant Day athletic teams.

---
